g2-implement.title: restate the prescriptive records: implement
g2-implement.imperative:
Fill templates/IMPLEMENTER_HANDOFF.template.md and dispatch constellation-implementer.

TASK: rewrite every prescriptive agent-supplied statement in episodes/active/ as a record of what happened, using ONLY the g1 `restate-assertion` op through scripts/apply_episode_delta.py --store-root episodes.

SCOPE: examine ALL 48 records in episodes/active/. The 32 pre-#447 records (issue-304-g3-* x5, issue-308-* x25, issue-309-* x2) are the ones in scope for rewriting. The 16 issue-447-* records are believed already to honour the constraint -- CHECK them and report the result, do not assume it. Report as "48 examined / 32 in scope / N restated".

THE WORDING STANDARD (Commander-set, this gate applies it): a statement is an OBSERVATION when it says what was done, by whom or by what, in the run being recorded -- past tense, a real subject, no second person, no forward-aimed modal. It is an INSTRUCTION when it is in imperative mood (a bare base-form verb opening a sentence or clause with no subject), addresses a reader (you, your), or carries a deontic modal aimed forward (must, should, always, never used as a directive).

ONE DELIBERATE EXEMPTION, DO NOT "FIX" IT: `task-intent` is written in the bare infinitive by house convention -- "Fix the STATE_NOTE-fallback wording gap..." is the form the store's own canonical worked record uses at docs/EPISODE_STORE.md:171. That is the format, not drift. Leave task-intent alone unless it addresses a reader in the second person.

WORKED CONTRAST from the issue, use it as the model:
  BEFORE (issue-308-001, prescriptive): "Give the harness the same fail-safe discipline as the production code under test: wrap per-iteration work in try/except with a guaranteed stop-signal in `finally`, and mark helper threads daemon=True as a backstop."
  AFTER-SHAPE (issue-447-005, observational): "The run paired each -k gate with an unfiltered whole-file and whole-suite run, and that pairing is what caught both defects."
Same information. No imperative mood, no second person, no forward-aimed modal.

HARD RULE -- DO NOT INVENT FACTS. Rewrite ONLY into what the record itself supports. Every episode carries task-intent, expected-behavior, observed-behavior and impact-cost alongside the workaround; use them to ground what actually happened. Where a statement's grounding does NOT support a factual rewrite -- typically because it was written as advice and the record never says whether it was applied -- LEAVE IT ALONE and list it in the result as UNGROUNDED, with the episode id, assertion id, and the specific reason the record cannot support a factual restatement. Reporting an ungrounded record is a correct outcome and g3 has an exception mechanism for exactly these; synthesising a past-tense claim the record cannot support is a falsification of the store and is the one unrecoverable failure of this gate.

ALSO CHECK, DO NOT SYNTHESISE: the other agent-supplied kinds (expected-behavior, observed-behavior, impact-cost) and the diagnosis assertions (suspected-cause, proposed-remedy) for the same drift. `proposed-remedy` is the one most likely to carry it. Restate the ones that plainly instruct AND are grounded; report the rest.

DOCTRINE CANDIDATES: several of these workarounds state what look like genuine rules. Collect each one -- episode id, assertion id, the rule as stated, and why it looks like doctrine -- into the IMPLEMENTER_RESULT for the human's decision. DO NOT write any of them into docs/agents/*, and DO NOT create any new file to hold them. That boundary is absolute.

EVIDENCE REQUIRED: the delta file(s) used, the writer invocations with --store-root episodes, the 48/32/N count, the UNGROUNDED list with reasons, the doctrine-candidate list, and `git diff --stat episodes/`.

g3-implement.title: the guard that can fail: implement
g3-implement.imperative:
Fill templates/IMPLEMENTER_HANDOFF.template.md and dispatch constellation-implementer.

TASK: ship something that CAN FAIL and that keeps episodes/active/ free of prescriptive statements going forward -- or return a measured honest null saying no command can do it reliably.

DELIVERABLE: scripts/verify_episode_observations.py plus tests/test_episode_observations.py.

SCOPE OF THE DETECTOR -- narrowed by measurement, do not widen it. A cold critic ran the naive three-trigger form over all 253 assertion statements in episodes/active/ and measured 41 imperative hits, 30 deontic-modal hits, 2 second-person hits -- roughly 65 flags against ~24 real defects. 31 of the 41 imperative hits were `task-intent`, which is bare-infinitive BY CONVENTION (docs/EPISODE_STORE.md:171 is the store's own canonical record in that form). Named false positives the naive form produced: issue-308-003 observed-behavior, issue-304-g3-005 suspected-cause, issue-308-010 observed-behavior ("A gate that MUST prove a refusal has no direct expression..." -- descriptive `must`), issue-309-002 expected-behavior ("...SHOULD exit 0" -- a recorded expectation).
So: apply the imperative rule ONLY to `workaround` and `proposed-remedy`. Apply the second-person rule to every kind. Do NOT match a bare modal anywhere -- the measurement shows `must`/`should` in this corpus are overwhelmingly descriptive or recorded expectations, not directives. Re-measure after narrowing and REPORT THE NUMBERS: flags before, flags after, false positives remaining, over all 253 statements.

THE EXCEPTION LIST, AND WHY IT EXISTS (cold-critic finding, load-bearing). g2 correctly leaves ungrounded prescriptive records alone. Those records are still prescriptive, so a guard that demands a clean store would go red on exactly the honest outcome, and the only escapes would be to fabricate a rewrite or to file the lexicon down until the corpus passes -- the checks-that-cannot-fail class this repo has a label for. So the guard carries an explicit exception list keyed by (episode id, assertion id) with a REQUIRED non-empty reason per entry, seeded from g2's UNGROUNDED list and from nothing else. The guard fails on any offender NOT on the list. It ALSO fails on a STALE entry -- one whose episode or assertion no longer exists, or that no longer trips any trigger -- so the list cannot quietly outlive its reason.

STRICT VS REPORT (cold-critic finding): --strict exits non-zero on any unlisted offender; the default exits 0 and prints the report. That is what lets the honest-null branch below ship without contradicting the red-proof.

THE MEASUREMENT THIS GATE OWES (LO-460 pre-ruling honest-null-on-the-check): run the detector over the 32 canon records as they were BEFORE the g2 rewrite -- recover them with `git show <pre-g2-sha>:episodes/active/<id>.md` into a temp store root; the Commander supplies <pre-g2-sha> in the handoff -- and over the corpus AFTER. Report the false-positive rate as a number, not an impression. If it makes the check unusable as a gate, SAY SO: report the honest null, ship report-only as the default, and state plainly that the invariant is routed to a named human rather than a machine. A measured negative is a complete deliverable here.

THE RED-PROOF, MANDATORY AND DOUBLE (LO-460 pre-ruling the-guard-must-be-able-to-fail): the guard must be OBSERVED REFUSING a record that plainly instructs, not merely observed passing. Ship BOTH:
  (r1) a test building a temp store whose one episode carries the pre-rewrite text of issue-308-001 verbatim -- "Give the harness the same fail-safe discipline as the production code under test: wrap per-iteration work in try/except with a guaranteed stop-signal in `finally`, and mark helper threads daemon=True as a backstop." -- asserting the guard exits NON-ZERO under --strict and NAMES that episode and assertion;
  (r2) a second red case whose text is NOT drawn from this corpus, so the detector cannot pass r1 by special-casing a known literal. Write a fresh plainly-instructing workaround of your own.
ALSO ship a committed red fixture store at .agent-work/r418-460/red-fixture/episodes/ (active/ + retired/, one plainly-instructing episode) built through apply_episode_delta.py, because the Commander runs the guard against it as an engine command postcondition at this gate's integrate step.

KEEPING IT TRUE GOING FORWARD (cold-critic finding): nothing currently registers this script anywhere, so without wiring it runs once and never again. tests/test_episode_observations.py MUST contain a test that runs the guard over the REAL episodes/ store root at repo root and asserts it is clean under --strict. That test is the delivery.

STATE THE HONEST LIMIT IN THE SCRIPT'S OWN DOCSTRING: this detector catches the MARKED forms of prescription. It cannot catch an unmarked one ("The right approach is to X"), the trigger lexicon is hand-maintained and will drift, and the kind-scoping above is a measured compromise rather than a general rule. Name that residue at the code site rather than letting the guard imply a completeness it does not have.

DO NOT create a file that accumulates advice for future agents. This is a verifier, not a playbook.
